critique.good: The team column is wide enough to keep team-name words intact, and the names form readable two-line row labels.
critique.problems: The P values split on every row, +28 splits, and GF, GA and Pts wrap in the header. These breaks make comparisons harder and give the header unnecessary height.
critique.cause: P is 41px wide but needs 42px; GD is 51px but needs 52px; GF, GA and Pts are each 1px short of their respective 43px, 45px and 48px minimums.

critique.good: P is wide enough to keep 28 on one line, and most team names remain readable on two lines.
critique.problems: Kingsbridge splits within the word, +28 splits, and GF, GA and Pts wrap. The split header makes the entire header row taller.
critique.cause: Team has 96px of content width, 1px less than the longest word needs. GD is 1px too narrow for +28, and GF, GA and Pts are each 1px too narrow for their headers.

critique.good: All headers and goal-difference values stay on one line, giving the statistical columns a clear hierarchy.
critique.problems: Every P value splits, and Kingsbridge and Harborough split within words. Harborough Wanderers consequently takes three lines, disrupting the row rhythm.
critique.cause: P is 1px short of the width needed for 28. Team has only 95px of content width, 2px short of the longest word; extra width in GF, GA, GD and Pts leaves too little for Team and P.

critique.good: The table fits the viewport, keeps every statistic and header on one line, and preserves whole words in team names. The consistent two-line rows make the standings easy to scan, while the shaded team column clearly identifies each row.
critique.problems: The team column feels tight, particularly around Kingsbridge and Harborough. Every team name wraps, so the table is tall despite having only seven teams. The narrow statistical columns are readable, though there is a little spare space in D, W and L.
critique.cause: At 118px, Team has only 97px of content width, exactly the stated width of the longest unbreakable word. D has 19px of content width against a 13px requirement; W and L each have 19px against an 18px requirement.

critique.good: The team column gives the names a clear identity, and wrapping them at spaces keeps each row readable. The statistical columns remain compact and the table fits the viewport.
critique.problems: P values split across lines in every row, the +28 goal difference splits, and the GF, GA and Pts headers wrap. These breaks interrupt comparisons and make the header as tall as the data rows.
critique.cause: The P, GF, GA, GD and Pts columns each have 1px less than the stated width needed for their longest content. The team column has 6px more than needed to keep its longest word intact.

understanding.purpose: Show league standings after 28 matches, with each team's results, goal record and points available for comparison.
understanding.reading: Readers scan down the team names and points to follow the standings, then across a row to understand a team's record. The narrow viewport leaves little spare width after keeping every word and number intact.
groups: Team identifies each row and needs substantially more space than the statistical columns.
P, W, D and L describe matches played and results.
GF, GA and GD describe goals scored, conceded and their difference.
Pts is the points total and a primary value for comparing standings.
keep_intact: Individual words in team names, especially Harborough and Wanderers.
All numeric values, including signs on goal differences.
may_wrap: Team names may wrap at spaces; longer names can use multiple lines while the statistics remain on one line.

bad.why: P values and +28 split across lines, and three headers break within their abbreviations.
Kingsbridge and +28 split within the word or number, and three headers break across lines.
P values split across lines, two team names break within words, and one team occupies three lines.
It duplicates r0A, including split P values, a split goal difference, and broken headers.
Although visually sound, its widths total 470px, exceeding the specified 469px maximum.

final.rationale: r1A keeps every abbreviation and number intact while wrapping each team name at a word boundary. Its compact header and consistent two-line team rows support scanning across the standings. The available width is almost entirely committed to preserving those qualities.

general: Keep numeric values and abbreviated headers intact so readers can scan and compare them quickly.
Allow names to wrap at word boundaries when that protects the readability of the data columns.
specific: The team column needs 118px to keep the longest unbreakable name intact with the specified padding.
The goal-difference column needs 52px to accommodate its widest value, while the played column needs 42px.

final.tradeoffs: The preferred design gives every team a two-line row and leaves little spare width. A designer might prefer more space around team names, but reclaiming it from the tightly fitted statistics risks broken values or headers.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates from the content widths and rendered candidates, not separately tested alternatives. Small reductions in W, D, or L may preserve legibility, though designers may differ on whether the altered spacing is equally balanced.

A.why: Team names wrap at word boundaries, but every P value splits across lines, as does +28; GF, GA and Pts also split. These breaks disrupt scanning.

B.why: The Team column is so narrow that its header and team names break within words over many lines, making row identification difficult and leaving large empty areas in the statistics columns.

C.why: Team names wrap cleanly at word boundaries, while all headers and numbers stay intact. The wider team column and compact statistics columns create a clear, consistent rhythm.

D.why: All words, headers and numbers remain intact, with a regular two-line rhythm for team names. The team column is tighter than in C, leaving long names close to its right edge.

reviews.unsure: C and D are close; the preference for C rests on the extra breathing room around the longest team names.

A.why: Team names wrap at word boundaries, but every P value breaks across two lines, as does +28; GF, GA and Pts also split in the header. This makes the statistics harder to scan.

B.why: The Team column is so narrow that its header and every team name break within words. The tall rows separate each name from its statistics and make comparisons difficult.

C.why: Team names wrap cleanly at word boundaries, while all headers and statistics stay intact. The compact numeric columns have a consistent rhythm and are easy to compare.

D.why: Team names wrap cleanly, and all headers and statistics remain intact. The slightly wider Team column gives row labels more breathing room while keeping the numeric columns compact.

reviews.unsure: C and D are very close; the small difference in column proportions does not materially change readability.
